ns2:section.sectionText: This course will review widely used models for choice decisions in detection, discrimination, and identification tasks. We will spend about half of the semester on signal-detection theory (SDT), a very simple probabilistic model of yes/no decision making that can be applied to a huge variety of tasks and easily extended to other common paradigms, including forced-choice responding. The remainder of the semester will be devoted to models related to SDT, including threshold models and individual choice theory, and also to accumulator models that describe both response times and accuracy (including the drift-diffusion model). This course will be useful for anyone who uses tasks (human or animal) that involve simple choice decision-making.
